chapter: Union, publishers, race and Harlem nightlife
title: Tommy Dorsey and Glenn Miller
summary: He finds both nice and good but not jazz; he recalls Dorsey refusing to sit next to him and meeting Miller at the Savoy.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: What about Tommy Dorsey and what was your impression of Tommy Dorsey and Glenn Miller? Did you think much of them?
I don't know nothing about (vulgarizations?) but they both are very nice guys.
How did you like their playing?
I think it's good. I know Tommy's good.

Both of them? Not too much. (LAUGHTER) No, that's right, because it's written down now. One O'Clock Jump, must be the first record when we started making these All Star records. I had the One O'Clock Jump and Tommy had the Bugle Call Rag. It's all written down in that book; you'll read it. He says, long as I play trombone I will never sit next to Jay C. Higginbotham and take a solo..and he had a whole quart of Grand Bad.
What about Glenn Miller? Did you have any -

No, I don't know that much about him. Never had a conversation with him. I met him when we were playing in the Savoy. You know we had the opposite band. We just say hello and shake hands and call it a day.
Glenn Miller was at the Savoy Ballroom?
